From 4ad79c874e53ebb7fe3b8ae7ac6c858a2121f415 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ben Horgan <ben.horgan@arm.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 18:27:16 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] arm_mpam: Fix null pointer dereference when restoring
 bandwidth counters

When an MSC supporting memory bandwidth monitoring is brought offline and
then online, mpam_restore_mbwu_state() calls __ris_msmon_read() via ipi to
restore the configuration of the bandwidth counters. It doesn't care about
the value read, mbwu_arg.val, and doesn't set it leading to a null pointer
dereference when __ris_msmon_read() adds to it. This results in a kernel
oops with a call trace such as:

Call trace:
__ris_msmon_read+0x19c/0x64c (P)
mpam_restore_mbwu_state+0xa0/0xe8
smp_call_on_cpu_callback+0x1c/0x38
process_one_work+0x154/0x4b4
worker_thread+0x188/0x310
kthread+0x11c/0x130
ret_from_fork+0x10/0x20

Provide a local variable for val to avoid __ris_msmon_read() dereferencing
a null pointer when adding to val.

Fixes: 41e8a14950e1 ("arm_mpam: Track bandwidth counter state for power management")
Signed-off-by: Ben Horgan <ben.horgan@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c b/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c
index 1eebc2602187..0666be6b0e88 100644
--- a/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c
+++ b/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c
@@ -1428,6 +1428,7 @@ static void mpam_reprogram_ris_partid(struct mpam_msc_ris *ris, u16 partid,
 static int mpam_restore_mbwu_state(void *_ris)
 {
 	int i;
+	u64 val;
 	struct mon_read mwbu_arg;
 	struct mpam_msc_ris *ris = _ris;
 	struct mpam_class *class = ris->vmsc->comp->class;
@@ -1437,6 +1438,7 @@ static int mpam_restore_mbwu_state(void *_ris)
 			mwbu_arg.ris = ris;
 			mwbu_arg.ctx = &ris->mbwu_state[i].cfg;
 			mwbu_arg.type = mpam_msmon_choose_counter(class);
+			mwbu_arg.val = &val;
 
 			__ris_msmon_read(&mwbu_arg);
 		}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

### Modifications per File

- **`drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c`**:  
  - Added a local variable `u64 val;` inside the function `mpam_restore_mbwu_state()`.  
  - Initialized the `mwbu_arg.val` field with the address of this variable (`mwbu_arg.val = &val;`) before calling `__ris_msmon_read()`.

### Relationships Between Changes

The bug was caused by `mwbu_arg.val` being left uninitialized (NULL pointer) while `__ris_msmon_read()` expects a valid pointer to store the read value. The addition of the `val` variable and its assignment to `mwbu_arg.val` provides a non‑null, writable memory location for the read operation, thereby preventing the null pointer dereference that led to the kernel oops. No other code depends on the stored value; the fix solely ensures memory safety.

Here is the commit message:
arm_mpam: Fix null pointer dereference when restoring
 bandwidth counters

When an MSC supporting memory bandwidth monitoring is brought offline and
then online, mpam_restore_mbwu_state() calls __ris_msmon_read() via ipi to
restore the configuration of the bandwidth counters. It doesn't care about
the value read, mbwu_arg.val, and doesn't set it leading to a null pointer
dereference when __ris_msmon_read() adds to it. This results in a kernel
oops with a call trace such as:

Call trace:
__ris_msmon_read+0x19c/0x64c (P)
mpam_restore_mbwu_state+0xa0/0xe8
smp_call_on_cpu_callback+0x1c/0x38
process_one_work+0x154/0x4b4
worker_thread+0x188/0x310
kthread+0x11c/0x130
ret_from_fork+0x10/0x20

Provide a local variable for val to avoid __ris_msmon_read() dereferencing
a null pointer when adding to val.

Fixes: 41e8a14950e1 ("arm_mpam: Track bandwidth counter state for power management")
Signed-off-by: Ben Horgan <ben.horgan@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
In `mpam_restore_mbwu_state()`, the `val` field of the `mon_read` structure (`mwbu_arg`) is not initialized, leaving it as a NULL pointer. When `__ris_msmon_read()` is called, it attempts to write the read value to the location pointed to by `mwbu_arg.val`, resulting in a null pointer dereference and kernel oops.

Here is the patch:
 /* Call with msc cfg_lock held */
 static int mpam_restore_mbwu_state(void *_ris)
 {
 	int i;
+	u64 val;
 	struct mon_read mwbu_arg;
 	struct mpam_msc_ris *ris = _ris;
 	struct mpam_class *class = ris->vmsc->comp->class;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ris->props.num_mbwu_mon; i++) {
 		if (ris->mbwu_state[i].enabled) {
 			mwbu_arg.ris = ris;
 			mwbu_arg.ctx = &ris->mbwu_state[i].cfg;
 			mwbu_arg.type = mpam_msmon_choose_counter(class);
+			mwbu_arg.val = &val;
 
 			__ris_msmon_read(&mwbu_arg);
 		}
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }
